findings.what: An existing same-session dispatch-ledger reader still treats a raw c.ok === true row as backing proof for ping-mode subprocess verification and never calls isVerifiedLivenessRecord or verifyRecord.
findings.why: testPing() can stamp subprocess_verified from exit0 + envelope + an unsigned/forged dispatch-completions row for the requested skill. The new liveness-read-choke-point guard scans scripts/dispatch, scripts/checks, scripts/sprint, scripts/warpos, and scripts/events, so this scripts/ root reader is outside the guard and the recurring unsigned ok:true reader class remains open.

findings.what: The structural guard considers a file verified if any verifier token appears anywhere in the file, rather than tying verification to each ok:true ledger predicate.
findings.why: A new same-session reader can import or mention isVerifiedLivenessRecord/verifyRecord and still gate on r.ok === true directly; the guard reports zero violations. I confirmed this with a synthetic reader. OK_PREDICATE also only catches .ok === true/.ok !== true, missing rec['ok'], destructured ok, and other equivalent same-session gates. The claim that a new reader cannot silently reopen the class is not delivered.

parsed.summary: Fail. The listed main readers mostly route through the new same-session liveness helper or verifyRecord, the cross-session sealed-capsule ceiling is not re-raised, and role-resolver appears env-inert for WARPOS_ACTOR_KIND/WARPOS_BOUND_ROLE. The blocking issues are a real missed same-session reader in scripts/skills-test.js and a guard implementation that can false-negative on straightforward new unverified reader variants.
